# netcup_server_disk_driver (Resource)

The storage driver of the disks of an existing netcup server (SCP REST API), one per server. netcup sets it for all disks at once. Changes are asynchronous; the provider waits for completion. `destroy` only drops the resource from state and the disks keep their driver.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netcup_server_disk_driver" "all" {
  server_id = 12345
  driver    = "VIRTIO_SCSI"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `driver` (String) Storage driver, `VIRTIO`, `VIRTIO_SCSI`, `IDE` or `SATA`. `netcup_server_disk_supported_drivers` lists those of the server.
- `server_id` (Number) Id of the server.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Equals `server_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import format: <server_id>
terraform import netcup_server_disk_driver.all 12345
```
